# rubrik_aws_cloud_native_application (Resource)

The `rubrik_aws_cloud_native_application` resource manages an AWS cloud native application, shown as a Cloud
Application in the RSC UI. An application groups the resources of one AWS account and region, so that their
configuration can be protected by an SLA Domain with the `AWS_CONFIG_OBJECT_TYPE` object type, and recovered to the
target account.

The AWS account must be onboarded with the `CLOUD_NATIVE_CONFIG_PROTECTION` feature in the application region, for
example using the `rubrik_aws_cnp_account` and `rubrik_aws_cnp_account_attachments` resources, and the feature must be
connected before the application can be created. RSC must also have finished discovering the account resources for
`resource_arns` to be accepted. The target account must be a
different AWS account, onboarded with the `CLOUD_NATIVE_CONFIG_PROTECTION` feature including the `RECOVERY`
permission groups, in the same region. RSC doesn't check the target account.

A resource joins the application when it carries any one of the `matching_tags`, or when it is listed in
`resource_arns`. RSC also includes the resources related to a tagged or listed resource, and those must not be
listed. A resource listed in `excluded_resource_arns` is left out, unless it's tightly coupled to an included one.

Assign the SLA Domain with the `rubrik_sla_domain_assignment` resource, using the application ID as the object ID.

-> **Note:** Changing `target_cloud_account_id` doesn't make recovery to the new account possible straight away. It
   becomes possible once the snapshots of the workloads have been replicated to it, after a full snapshot cycle.

~> **Warning:** RSC refuses to delete an application while it has config snapshots. Set
   `delete_snapshots_on_destroy` to `true` and apply before destroying the application, or wait for the snapshots to
   expire. The `CLOUD_NATIVE_CONFIG_PROTECTION` feature can't be removed from an AWS account which is the source or
   the target of an application.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# The source and the target AWS accounts, both onboarded with the
# CLOUD_NATIVE_CONFIG_PROTECTION feature. See the rubrik_aws_cnp_account
# resource for the full onboarding, including the IAM roles.
resource "rubrik_aws_cnp_account" "source" {
  name      = "production"
  native_id = "123456789012"
  regions   = ["us-east-1"]

  feature {
    name              = "CLOUD_DISCOVERY"
    permission_groups = ["BASIC"]
  }
  feature {
    name              = "CLOUD_NATIVE_CONFIG_PROTECTION"
    permission_groups = ["BASIC", "BASIC_2", "RECOVERY", "RECOVERY_2", "RECOVERY_3", "RECOVERY_4"]
  }
}

resource "rubrik_aws_cnp_account" "recovery" {
  name      = "recovery"
  native_id = "210987654321"
  regions   = ["us-east-1"]

  feature {
    name              = "CLOUD_DISCOVERY"
    permission_groups = ["BASIC"]
  }
  feature {
    name              = "CLOUD_NATIVE_CONFIG_PROTECTION"
    permission_groups = ["BASIC", "BASIC_2", "RECOVERY", "RECOVERY_2", "RECOVERY_3", "RECOVERY_4"]
  }
}

# The application holds the resources tagged Application = web-store, plus
# one explicitly listed Lambda function.
resource "rubrik_aws_cloud_native_application" "web_store" {
  name                    = "web-store"
  cloud_account_id        = rubrik_aws_cnp_account.source.id
  target_cloud_account_id = rubrik_aws_cnp_account.recovery.id
  region                  = "us-east-1"

  matching_tags = {
    Application = "web-store"
  }
  resource_arns = [
    "arn:aws:lambda:us-east-1:123456789012:function:web-store-checkout",
  ]
}

# Protect the application configuration with an SLA Domain.
resource "rubrik_sla_domain" "cloud_applications" {
  name         = "cloud-applications"
  object_types = ["AWS_CONFIG_OBJECT_TYPE"]

  hourly_schedule {
    frequency      = 6
    retention      = 7
    retention_unit = "DAYS"
  }
}

resource "rubrik_sla_domain_assignment" "web_store" {
  sla_domain_id = rubrik_sla_domain.cloud_applications.id
  object_ids    = [rubrik_aws_cloud_native_application.web_store.id]
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `cloud_account_id` (String) RSC cloud account ID (UUID) of the AWS account the application lives in. The account must be onboarded with the `CLOUD_NATIVE_CONFIG_PROTECTION` feature. Changing this forces a new resource to be created.
- `name` (String) Application name. Must be unique and consist of letters, digits, `-` and `_`, at most 1024 characters.
- `region` (String) AWS region of the application. Changing this forces a new resource to be created.
- `target_cloud_account_id` (String) RSC cloud account ID (UUID) of the AWS account the application is recovered to. Must differ from `cloud_account_id`.

### Optional

- `delete_snapshots_on_destroy` (Boolean) Delete the config snapshots of the application when the resource is destroyed. RSC refuses to delete an application with config snapshots. When `true`, the application is set to Do Not Protect with its snapshots expiring immediately, and destroy waits for the snapshots to be gone. The snapshots of the workloads in the application are not affected. Default is `false`.
- `excluded_resource_arns` (Set of String) ARNs of resources excluded from the application, even when tagged or related to an included resource. A resource tightly coupled to an included one can't be excluded.
- `matching_tags` (Map of String) AWS tags, as key value pairs. A resource carrying any one of the tags joins the application. At most 3 tags. Once set, the tags can be changed but not all removed. At least one of `matching_tags` and `resource_arns` must be specified.
- `resource_arns` (Set of String) ARNs of resources explicitly included in the application. Each resource must have been discovered by RSC in the account and region, and its service must be enabled. Tagged resources, and resources related to the listed ones, are included by RSC and must not be listed.
- `services` (Set of String) AWS services whose resources are protected. Possible values are `EC2`, `ECR`, `ECS`, `EKS`, `ELASTICACHE`, `ELB`, `LAMBDA`, `RDS`, `S3`, `SECRETS_MANAGER`. Default is all of them. VPCs, IAM roles and Route 53 hosted zones are always included.
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Application ID (UUID). Also the object ID when assigning an SLA Domain to the application.
- `protection_status` (String) Protection status of the application.
- `refresh_status` (String) Status of the last refresh of the application resources.

<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `delete` (String) How long to wait for the config snapshots to be deleted when `delete_snapshots_on_destroy` is `true`. Default is `20m0s`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `identity` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = rubrik_aws_cloud_native_application.web_store
  identity = {
    id = "9a8a7c63-0ae4-4be8-b0a2-1ab8b28a4f45"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
### Identity Schema

#### Required

- `id` (String) Application ID (UUID).

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = rubrik_aws_cloud_native_application.web_store
  id = "9a8a7c63-0ae4-4be8-b0a2-1ab8b28a4f45"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
% terraform import rubrik_aws_cloud_native_application.web_store 9a8a7c63-0ae4-4be8-b0a2-1ab8b28a4f45
```
